linux.reason: Pinned core-info identifies the core but does not establish a current host-specific package; RetroArch frontend presence alone is not package evidence.

linux-flatpak.reason: The installed RetroArch Flatpak-updater core was loaded and executed through exact-hash input and state oracles on the Linux host.

macos.reason: The official Libretro macOS arm64 buildbot artifact was downloaded and executed on an Apple Silicon host.

windows.reason: The official Libretro Windows x86_64 buildbot artifact and DLL identity were verified on a GitHub-hosted Windows Server 2025 VM; feature execution remained separately blocked by unavailable game content.
evidence: identity:2026-09-13 GitHub-hosted Windows Server 2025 x86_64 identity audit: the official Libretro archive matched pinned sha256 77d38183ba995e8bb3e2f514e680d30645eae3b8aad78d6b62026d166c664590, and its MAME 0.289 (4fc9a931) DLL matched sha256 b38c9ebb2cf679745701569c511f9c381e1f4f3f43e0212fe728397b0badbead plus the expected full-path/block-extract metadata.

controller.mapping_summary: Catalog retropad profiles map the system controls to the core’s libretro input ports.

firmware.notes: mame_libretro.info supplies the canonical firmware paths and optionality; hashes are included only where the pinned notes publish them.

saves.naming: The pinned core-info metadata declares libretro_saves=false; no standalone RetroArch persistent save artifact is claimed.

states.naming: <content-basename>.state for slot 0 and <content-basename>.stateN for numbered slots; RetroArch may place these under its configured states directory.
